description:
The below details the standard actuarial methods to develop claims.
In general where a year has little claims experience (i.e. more recent years) then benchmarks are relied upon.
As more experience is available then relying purely on experience is more appropriate.

True exposure rating method. Assumes the year will develop according to a benchmark loss ratio (e.g. if the benchmark loss ratio for attritional claims is 40% and the premium is $1m then the estimate of claims is $0.4m)

Exposure/experience rating method. Weights between the chain ladder and IELR. The weight is the % developed the year is assumed to be. For example if a year is 50% developed then 50% weight is placed towards the chain ladder and 50% to the IELR method.

True experience rating method. Assumes the year will develop according to a development pattern of claims. For example if a year has $0.5m of incurred claims and is assumed to be 80% developed then the estimate of ultimate claims is $0.5m/0.8 = $0.625m
